title: Story 27: Backend-First Dependency Chain
pmResponse:
# Story 27: Backend-First Dependency Chain — Complete Action Plan

## Situation Analysis

The product owner has requested real-time order tracking via live updates (prepared → picked up → delivered). This requires **WebSocket integration**, which introduces a critical architectural constraint: unlike REST endpoints, WebSocket connections cannot be reliably mocked. The frontend Android app needs a **live, running backend on staging** to develop and test against.

This is fundamentally different from Story 21's pattern where the frontend only needed the API contract (a document) to begin work. Here, the frontend must wait for the full backend pipeline: Plan → Dev → Validate → **Deploy to Staging**, and only then can frontend work begin.

---

## Phase 1: Create the Parent Epic

This is a product-owner request routed through the PM. Since it comes from management, it auto-accepts (no review needed). I create the epic first so all children can reference it as a parent.

```bash
agt create "Real-Time Order Tracking — Live Order Status via WebSocket" \
  --description "Customers see live updates as their order moves through stages: preparing, prepared, picked_up, in_transit, delivered. Requires WebSocket integration for real-time push updates. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: Frontend cannot mock WebSocket connections and requires a deployed backend on staging before development can begin. This is a strict backend-first dependency chain, unlike Story 21 where frontend only needed the API contract." \
  --tags epic \
  --assignee product-owner \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2
```

**Reasoning:** The epic is the top-level container owned by the product-owner (they own the product decision and will do acceptance review). Priority 2 reflects high business value. Status is `todo` — nothing has started yet. I note the `#EPIC` ID from output for all child creations.

---

## Phase 2: Create Backend Issues (Sequential Chain — Plan → Dev → Validate → Release)

These four issues form the backend pipeline that MUST complete before any frontend work begins.

### B1 — Backend Planning

```bash
agt create "Design WebSocket Order Tracking API — Connection Protocol, Event Schema, and Lifecycle" \
  --description "Architect the real-time order tracking WebSocket system. Define: (1) WebSocket endpoint and connection handshake, (2) Authentication/authorization for socket connections (token-based), (3) Event message schema for order status changes: preparing, prepared, picked_up, in_transit, delivered, (4) Connection lifecycle: heartbeat/ping-pong, reconnection strategy, graceful disconnect, (5) Database schema changes for order status tracking with timestamps, (6) How order status transitions are triggered (from kitchen/courier systems). Output: API contract document and database migration plan." \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee backend-architect \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Backend planning phase. The architect designs the full contract — this is where the WebSocket protocol, message format, and lifecycle are specified. Priority 2 because this is the critical-path starting point. No blockers — this can start immediately.

### B2 — Backend Development

```bash
agt create "Implement WebSocket Order Tracking Backend — Server, Event Broadcasting, and Order Status Management" \
  --description "Implement the WebSocket order tracking system per the architect's design: (1) WebSocket server endpoint with auth handshake, (2) Order status event broadcaster — push updates when status changes, (3) Connection manager with heartbeat and reconnection support, (4) Database models/migrations for order status with timestamps, (5) Integration points with kitchen/courier systems to trigger status updates, (6) Unit tests for all components." \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee backend-developer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Backend development phase. Blocked by B1 (needs the design before implementing). Priority 3 since it's queued behind B1.

### B3 — Backend Validation

```bash
agt create "Validate WebSocket Order Tracking API — Connection Tests, Load Tests, and Reconnection Behavior" \
  --description "Validate the WebSocket backend: (1) Connection establishment and authentication tests, (2) Verify all order status events are correctly pushed (preparing, prepared, picked_up, in_transit, delivered), (3) Load test concurrent WebSocket connections (target: 500+ simultaneous), (4) Reconnection and failover behavior, (5) Message ordering and delivery guarantees, (6) Security: unauthorized connections rejected, token expiry handling. Must confirm the service is stable enough for staging deployment." \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee backend-validator \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Backend validation phase. Blocked by B2. The validator must confirm the WebSocket service is production-quality before it goes to staging, since the frontend team will depend on it.

### B4 — Deploy WebSocket Service to Staging

```bash
agt create "Deploy WebSocket Order Tracking Service to Staging Environment" \
  --description "Deploy the validated WebSocket service to staging: (1) Configure WebSocket support on staging load balancer/reverse proxy (sticky sessions or WebSocket-aware proxy), (2) Deploy service with health checks, (3) Configure connection timeouts and keepalive settings, (4) Verify staging endpoint is accessible and accepting connections from external clients (critical for Android app testing), (5) Smoke test: connect, receive a test event, disconnect. This deployment is the GATE that unblocks the frontend team — it must be verified working before notifying android-developer." \
  --tags chore \
  --assignee devops-engineer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Backend release phase. This is the **critical milestone** — the entire frontend chain is blocked until this completes. I emphasize in the description that this deployment unblocks the frontend team and must include external accessibility verification. Tagged `chore` since it's infrastructure/deployment work, not a feature itself.

---

## Phase 3: Create Frontend Issues (Plan → Dev → Style → Validate)

These issues cannot start until B4 is complete. The frontend team will be idle during backend development — I document this explicitly.

### F1 — Frontend Planning

```bash
agt create "Plan Android Order Tracking Screen Integration Against Live Staging WebSocket" \
  --description "Plan the Android implementation of real-time order tracking: (1) Design WebSocket client architecture (connection manager, reconnection logic, message deserialization), (2) Plan the order tracking screen UI — map view, status timeline (preparing → prepared → picked_up → in_transit → delivered), live ETA, (3) Define how to bind WebSocket events to UI state (LiveData/Flow/StateFlow), (4) Plan background service for maintaining connection when app is backgrounded, (5) Test plan against staging endpoint. NOTE: This planning can only happen AFTER the backend is deployed to staging — the team needs to test actual connection behavior, message formats, and reconnection patterns against the real service." \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee android-developer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Frontend planning phase. The android-developer handles both planning and development for frontend features. The description explicitly states WHY this can't start until staging is live — this documents the architectural rationale.

### F2 — Frontend Development

```bash
agt create "Build Order Tracking Screen with WebSocket Client — Live Status Updates and Map Integration" \
  --description "Implement the Android order tracking feature: (1) WebSocket client with connection management, automatic reconnection, and heartbeat, (2) Order tracking screen with live status timeline (preparing, prepared, picked_up, in_transit, delivered), (3) Map integration showing courier location (if applicable), (4) Push notifications for major status transitions, (5) Background connection handling, (6) Error states: connection lost, reconnection in progress, order not found. Test against staging WebSocket endpoint throughout development." \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee android-developer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Frontend development phase. Blocked by F1 (planning must come first). The developer builds against the live staging backend throughout — this is the core reason for the backend-first chain.

### F3 — Frontend Styling

```bash
agt create "Style Order Tracking Screen — Material Design, Animations, and Accessibility" \
  --description "Apply Material Design 3 to the order tracking screen: (1) Animated status timeline with smooth transitions between order stages, (2) Progress indicators and skeleton loading states, (3) Map UI polish with custom markers and route animation, (4) Accessibility: screen reader support for live status updates, sufficient color contrast, touch target sizing, (5) Responsive layouts for different screen sizes, (6) Dark mode support." \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee android-designer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Frontend styling phase — per the team flow, styling happens AFTER the developer builds the functional screen. Blocked by F2. The designer needs a working screen to style.

### F4 — Frontend Validation

```bash
agt create "Validate Order Tracking UI — Real-Time Update Tests, Cross-Device Testing, and Bug Reproduction" \
  --description "Validate the Android order tracking feature: (1) Verify all order status events display correctly in real-time against staging backend, (2) Test reconnection behavior: kill connection, verify auto-reconnect and no duplicate/missed events, (3) Cross-device testing: phone, tablet, different Android versions (min SDK to latest), (4) Background/foreground transition behavior, (5) Performance: memory leaks during long connections, battery impact, (6) Push notification delivery and accuracy, (7) Accessibility audit." \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee android-validator \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Frontend validation phase. Blocked by F3. The validator specifically tests the real-time behavior against the staging backend — this is only possible because the backend is deployed.

---

## Phase 4: Create Release Issues

### R1 — Backend Production Deployment (parallel with frontend work)

```bash
agt create "Deploy WebSocket Order Tracking Service to Production" \
  --description "Deploy the validated WebSocket service to production: (1) Production load balancer WebSocket configuration, (2) Deploy with canary rollout, (3) Configure monitoring and alerting for WebSocket connection counts, message throughput, error rates, (4) Set up connection drain for zero-downtime deployments, (5) Verify production endpoint. This can proceed in parallel with frontend development since the frontend is testing against staging. Must complete before Play Store submission." \
  --tags chore \
  --assignee devops-engineer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Backend production deployment. This is blocked by B4 (staging deploy) but NOT blocked by frontend work — it can proceed in parallel. This is a key PM optimization: the backend goes to prod while the frontend team builds against staging. Must complete before Play Store release (R3) so the backend is live when customers get the app.

### R2 — Build Release APK

```bash
agt create "Build Signed Release APK for Order Tracking Feature" \
  --description "Build the production release APK: (1) Final QA sign-off, (2) Build signed release APK/AAB with production config, (3) Point to production backend endpoints (not staging), (4) Verify no staging/test code in release build, (5) Generate release notes for Play Store." \
  --tags chore \
  --assignee android-developer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Per team flow, the android-developer builds the release APK after validation passes. Blocked by F4.

### R3 — Play Store Submission

```bash
agt create "Submit Order Tracking Update to Play Store" \
  --description "Submit the release to Google Play Store: (1) Upload AAB to Play Console, (2) Complete store listing updates (screenshots of new tracking screen), (3) Submit for review, (4) Monitor review status. NOTE: If rejected, follow Play Store rejection workflow — do NOT attempt to force release." \
  --tags chore \
  --assignee devops-engineer \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3 \
  --parentId <EPIC_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** Per team flow, devops handles Play Store submission. Blocked by BOTH R1 (backend must be live in prod) and R2 (APK must be built). I note the Play Store rejection contingency per the team rules.

---

## Phase 5: Set Up Blockages (Dependency Chain)

All issues are now created. I set up the blockage chain to enforce the strict sequential ordering.

### Backend Internal Chain

```bash
# B2 blocked by B1 — can't implement without the design
agt blockages add <B2_ID> --by <B1_ID>

# B3 blocked by B2 — can't validate what isn't built
agt blockages add <B3_ID> --by <B2_ID>

# B4 blocked by B3 — can't deploy what hasn't passed validation
agt blockages add <B4_ID> --by <B3_ID>
```

### ⚠️ CRITICAL BLOCKAGE: Frontend Blocked on Deployed Backend (NOT Contract)

```bash
# F1 blocked by B4 — THE KEY DEPENDENCY
# Frontend planning cannot start until the backend is DEPLOYED TO STAGING
# This is different from Story 21 where frontend only needed the contract document
agt blockages add <F1_ID> --by <B4_ID>
```

**Reasoning:** This is the defining blockage of this story. In Story 21, the frontend was blocked on the API *contract* (a document from planning). Here, the frontend is blocked on the *deployed running service* because WebSocket connections cannot be mocked. This enforces the strict backend-first chain.

### Frontend Internal Chain

```bash
# F2 blocked by F1 — can't build without a plan
agt blockages add <F2_ID> --by <F1_ID>

# F3 blocked by F2 — designer needs a working screen to style
agt blockages add <F3_ID> --by <F2_ID>

# F4 blocked by F3 — validator tests the styled, finished screen
agt blockages add <F4_ID> --by <F3_ID>
```

### Release Chain

```bash
# R1 blocked by B4 — prod deploy after staging deploy (can run parallel with frontend)
agt blockages add <R1_ID> --by <B4_ID>

# R2 blocked by F4 — APK build after frontend validation passes
agt blockages add <R2_ID> --by <F4_ID>

# R3 blocked by BOTH R1 and R2 — Play Store submission requires live backend AND built APK
agt blockages add <R3_ID> --by <R1_ID> <R2_ID>
```

---

## Phase 6: Add Context Comments

### Comment on the Epic — Strategy Documentation

```bash
agt comments add <EPIC_ID> --content "PM STRATEGY NOTE — Backend-First Dependency Chain

This feature requires WebSocket integration for real-time order status updates. Unlike REST APIs, WebSocket connections cannot be reliably mocked — the frontend needs a live, running backend to develop and test against.

DECISION: Strict sequential chain. The full backend pipeline (Plan → Dev → Validate → Deploy to Staging) must complete BEFORE any frontend work begins.

This is explicitly different from Story 21 (API contract joint planning) where the frontend only needed the contract document to start work. Here, the frontend cannot proceed without the deployed staging service because:
1. WebSocket reconnection behavior must be tested against a real server
2. Message timing and ordering can't be simulated with mocks
3. Connection lifecycle (heartbeat, timeout, drain) requires a live endpoint
4. The team needs to discover real-world latency and failure modes during development

OPTIMIZATION: Backend production deployment (R1) can proceed in parallel with frontend development (F1-F4) since the frontend tests against staging. This minimizes total timeline.

Critical path: B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → F1 → F2 → F3 → F4 → R2 → R3
Parallel: R1 runs alongside F1-F4 (blocked only by B4)

Assigned to product-owner for final acceptance review upon completion."
```

### Comment on B1 — Kickoff Directive

```bash
agt comments add <B1_ID> --content "This is the critical-path starting point. The entire feature chain (backend + frontend + release) is blocked until this design is complete. Please prioritize.

Key deliverables needed: WebSocket endpoint spec, event message schema (JSON), auth mechanism, reconnection protocol, database migration plan, and integration points with kitchen/courier status systems.

The frontend team (android-developer) will review your output as part of their own planning (F1), so please document the connection protocol thoroughly."
```

### Comment on B4 — Staging Gate Significance

```bash
agt comments add <B4_ID> --content "⚠️ CRITICAL MILESTONE: This staging deployment is the gate that unblocks the entire frontend team. Until this issue is resolved, the android-developer, android-designer, and android-validator are all idle.

Requirements before marking complete:
1. WebSocket endpoint is accessible from external clients (not just localhost)
2. A successful test connection has been made and a test event received
3. Load balancer/proxy is configured for WebSocket upgrades
4. Connection keepalive/timeout settings are production-appropriate

Once verified, notify the PM immediately so we can kick off F1 (frontend planning)."
```

### Comment on F1 — Dependency Rationale

```bash
agt comments add <F1_ID> --content "NOTE FOR ANDROID DEVELOPER: This task is blocked until the backend WebSocket service is deployed to staging (B4). You cannot start earlier because:

- WebSocket connections cannot be mocked like REST endpoints
- You need to test real connection behavior, reconnection patterns, and message timing against the live service
- The frontend plan must account for actual backend behavior discovered through testing

This is different from Story 21 where you could start with just the API contract. Here, you need the running service.

When B4 is complete, you'll connect to the staging WebSocket endpoint, test the connection protocol, and then plan your implementation approach based on real behavior."
```

### Comment on R1 — Parallelization Opportunity

```bash
agt comments add <R1_ID> --content "PM NOTE: This production deployment is NOT on the critical path — it can proceed in parallel with frontend development (F1-F4). The frontend tests against staging, not production. 

However, this MUST complete before the Play Store submission (R3) so that the backend is live when customers receive the app update. Recommend starting this as soon as B4 (staging deploy) is complete to maximize parallelism."
```

### Comment on R3 — Release Coordination

```bash
agt comments add <R3_ID> --content "This is the final gate. Requires both: (1) Backend deployed to production (R1) and (2) Release APK built and validated (R2). 

Timeline coordination: Backend production deploy and Android APK build happen in parallel after their respective chains complete. Play Store review can take 1-3 days — factor this into delivery estimates to the product owner.

If Play Store rejects the submission, follow the non-standard rejection workflow — do NOT attempt to bypass the review process."
```

---

## Phase 7: Initial Status Updates

```bash
# Move the epic to in-progress — active planning and breakdown is underway
agt update <EPIC_ID> --status in-progress
```

**Reasoning:** The epic moves to `in-progress` because the PM has completed breakdown and the first work item (B1) is ready to be picked up. The team is actively engaged.

B1 remains `todo` — it's ready for backend-architect to pick up. When the architect begins, they (or the PM) will move it to `in-progress`.

---

## Complete Issue Hierarchy (Final State)

```
#EPIC  Real-Time Order Tracking — Live Order Status via WebSocket [epic, in-progress, product-owner, P2]
│
├── #B1  Design WebSocket Order Tracking API [feature, todo, backend-architect, P2]
│        ↳ READY TO START — no blockers
│
├── #B2  Implement WebSocket Order Tracking Backend [feature, todo, backend-developer, P3]
│        ↳ BLOCKED by #B1
│
├── #B3  Validate WebSocket Order Tracking API [feature, todo, backend-validator, P3]
│        ↳ BLOCKED by #B2
│
├── #B4  Deploy WebSocket Service to Staging [chore, todo, devops-engineer, P3]
│        ↳ BLOCKED by #B3
│        ↳ ⚠️ CRITICAL GATE — unblocks entire frontend chain
│
├── #F1  Plan Android Order Tracking Integration [feature, todo, android-developer, P3]
│        ↳ BLOCKED by #B4  ◄── KEY: blocked on DEPLOYED BACKEND, not just contract
│
├── #F2  Build Order Tracking Screen & WebSocket Client [feature, todo, android-developer, P3]
│        ↳ BLOCKED by #F1
│
├── #F3  Style Order Tracking Screen [feature, todo, android-designer, P3]
│        ↳ BLOCKED by #F2
│
├── #F4  Validate Order Tracking UI & Real-Time Updates [feature, todo, android-validator, P3]
│        ↳ BLOCKED by #F3
│
├── #R1  Deploy Backend to Production [chore, todo, devops-engineer, P3]
│        ↳ BLOCKED by #B4  (runs in PARALLEL with F1-F4)
│
├── #R2  Build Release APK for Order Tracking [chore, todo, android-developer, P3]
│        ↳ BLOCKED by #F4
│
└── #R3  Submit Order Tracking to Play Store [chore, todo, devops-engineer, P3]
         ↳ BLOCKED by #R1 AND #R2
```

### Critical Path (Longest Chain)

```
B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → F1 → F2 → F3 → F4 → R2 → R3
 └──── Backend (4 steps) ────┘└──── Frontend (4 steps) ────┘└ Release ┘
```

### Parallel Track

```
B4 → R1  (backend prod deploy, runs alongside frontend work)
```

---

## Phase 8: Ongoing Monitoring Actions (As Work Progresses)

As the PM, I would monitor and execute these updates as milestones are reached:

### When B1 completes:
```bash
agt update <B1_ID> --status done
# Resolve the blockage on B2
agt blockages resolve <B2_ID> --by <B1_ID>
# Notify backend-developer
agt comments add <B2_ID> --content "B1 complete. API contract is ready. You're unblocked — please begin implementation."
```

### When B4 (staging deploy) completes — CRITICAL MILESTONE:
```bash
agt update <B4_ID> --status done
# Resolve frontend blockage — the key moment
agt blockages resolve <F1_ID> --by <B4_ID>
# Also unblock R1 (prod deploy can start in parallel)
agt blockages resolve <R1_ID> --by <B4_ID>
# Kick off frontend
agt comments add <F1_ID> --content "🟢 Backend is live on staging! WebSocket endpoint verified. You're unblocked — please begin frontend planning. Staging endpoint: [URL]"
# Kick off parallel prod deploy
agt comments add <R1_ID> --content "Staging deploy complete and verified. You're unblocked to begin production deployment in parallel with frontend development."
```

### When F4 (frontend validation) completes:
```bash
agt update <F4_ID> --status done
agt blockages resolve <R2_ID> --by <F4_ID>
agt comments add <R2_ID> --content "Frontend validation passed. Build the release APK pointing to production endpoints."
```

### When R1 AND R2 complete:
```bash
agt blockages resolve <R3_ID> --by <R1_ID> <R2_ID>
agt comments add <R3_ID> --content "Both backend production and release APK are ready. Submit to Play Store."
```

### When R3 completes (Play Store approval):
```bash
agt update <R3_ID> --status done
# Close the epic
agt update <EPIC_ID> --status closed
agt comments add <EPIC_ID> --content "✅ Feature shipped. Real-time order tracking is live in production. All issues resolved. Forwarding to product-owner for acceptance review."
```

---

## Summary of Key PM Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| **Strict backend-first chain** | WebSocket connections can't be mocked; frontend needs live staging backend |
| **F1 blocked on B4 (deploy), not B1 (contract)** | This is the defining difference from Story 21 — frontend needs the running service, not just the design doc |
| **R1 (prod deploy) parallelized with frontend** | PM optimization — backend goes to prod while frontend builds against staging, minimizing total timeline |
| **R3 blocked by both R1 and R2** | Backend must be live in prod AND APK must be built before Play Store submission |
| **Frontend team idle during backend phase** | Acknowledged and documented; no workaround given the WebSocket constraint |
| **B4 includes external accessibility verification** | Ensures the Android app can actually reach the staging WebSocket endpoint before declaring unblock |
feedback: Major structural gaps. The agent used a flat single-epic structure instead of the required 4-level hierarchy (Initiative -> Epic -> Feature -> Task) with separate Backend and Frontend epics. It mis-tagged all phase work as `feature` instead of `task`, skipped the Feature level entirely, and never created an Initiative. Critically, it created ZERO sync trackers (`task,sync` assigned to project-manager) -- the entire sync/verification pattern is absent, so the cross-epic dependency is wired to B4 directly rather than a backend sync tracker. The agent also missed the architecture agreement loop: no android-developer review task, no PM 'verify agreed' sync before implementation, violating the key behavior that the consumer reviews the protocol and the PM reads that review. Strengths: it correctly identified the headline behavior -- frontend is blocked on the backend's STAGING DEPLOYMENT (not just the contract), explicitly contrasted this with Story 21, and got most worker agent assignments right (architect/design, developer/implement, validator, devops/deploy, android roles). But it assigned the epic to product-owner instead of project-manager, and added unrequested release tasks (production deploy, APK build, Play Store) while omitting core required pieces.
